tools.description:
Read the content of a file from NextCloud.

For photos, screenshots and other images, use nc_webdav_view_image
instead: it shows you the image itself, while this tool returns it as
base64 text or OCR output.

Raises ``ToolError`` when ``EXCLUDED_TAGS`` is configured and the
file (or an ancestor folder) carries an excluded system tag.

Args:
    path: Full path to the file to read
    parse_document: How to handle a document (PDF, DOCX, image, ...):

        - ``"auto"`` (default): extract its text. Cheapest route that
          works -- a PDF with a good text layer is read directly, and a
          scanned one escalates to OCR when the server has OCR enabled.
        - ``"markdown"``: additionally reconstruct structure (headings,
          tables) rather than returning a flat text layer. Costs a
          second, slower parse and is bounded by a page ceiling, when it
          cannot be honoured the response says so instead of pretending.
        - ``"raw"``: do not parse. Text files are decoded, anything else
          comes back base64-encoded.

        Files no processor handles (plain text, JSON, archives) are
        unaffected by this argument.
    page_start: PDF only. First page to read (1-based). Omit it, and
        page_end, to read the whole document. Use a range for a long
        PDF: only those pages are parsed and returned, which is faster
        and keeps the response to a size you can use. The markdown page
        ceiling then counts only the requested pages.
    page_end: PDF only. Last page to read (1-based, inclusive). Omitted
        means through the last page. A value past the end is clamped to
        the last page and noted in parse_notes. Neither argument can be
        combined with parse_document="raw".
    line_start: Text files only. First line to read (1-based). Use a
        line range to look at part of a long text file instead of
        loading all of it, for example to find the passage to change
        with nc_webdav_edit_file. Cannot be combined with page_start or
        page_end.
    line_end: Text files only. Last line to read (1-based, inclusive).
        Omitted means through the last line. A value past the end is
        clamped. ``total_lines`` in the response says how long the file
        is. A single line longer than the response limit is returned
        cut off, and parse_notes says so.
    line_numbers: Prefix each returned line with its number and a tab,
        for a line-range read. Strip that prefix again before quoting
        text in nc_webdav_edit_file.

Returns:
    ``ReadFileResponse``. Alongside ``path``/``content``/``content_type``/
    ``size``/``etag`` it always describes what you are actually holding:

    - ``parse_status``: ``parsed`` / ``failed`` / ``skipped`` /
      ``not_applicable``.
    - ``content_format``: ``markdown``, ``text`` or ``base64``.
    - ``parse_tier`` / ``parse_processor``: which extraction tier
      produced the content (``fast``, ``structured``, ``ocr``).
    - ``parse_notes``: **if this is non-empty, tell the user what
      degraded** (OCR unavailable, structure not reconstructed, size cap,
      parse failure) rather than presenting the content as the complete
      document.
    - ``etag``: pass this back into ``nc_webdav_write_file``'s
      ``if_match`` when writing this same path later, so a manual edit
      made elsewhere in the meantime (e.g. in the Nextcloud web UI) is
      detected as a conflict instead of silently overwritten.
    - ``url``: a link that opens the file in Nextcloud. Offer it when
      reporting on the file, and especially when ``parse_notes`` says
      the extraction degraded.
    - ``page_count``: total pages in a parsed PDF. With ``page_start``/
      ``page_end`` (the pages actually returned) it tells you whether
      more remains to read.
tools.name: nc_webdav_read_file

tools.description:
Write content to a file in NextCloud.

To change part of an existing text file, use nc_webdav_edit_file
instead: it takes only the passage to replace, not the whole file.

Writes are **fail-closed**: an existing file is never silently
overwritten. What happens depends on ``if_match`` (see below).

Raises ``ToolError`` when ``EXCLUDED_TAGS`` is configured and the
target path (or an ancestor folder) carries an excluded system tag,
when the decoded content exceeds ``WEBDAV_WRITE_MAX_MB``, when the
write conflicts with a concurrent edit or an existing/missing file
(412), or when the file is locked by another client (423) -- see
``if_match`` below.

Args:
    path: Full path where to write the file
    content: File content (text or base64 for binary)
    content_type: MIME type (auto-detected if not provided, use 'type;base64' for binary)
    if_match: Controls overwrite safety.
        - Omit (``None``) to **create a new file**: the write fails
          with a ``ToolError`` if the path already exists. To change an
          existing file you must first read it with
          ``nc_webdav_read_file`` and pass the etag it returned.
        - Pass that **etag** to overwrite the file only if it has not
          changed since you read it. If someone edited it in the
          meantime (e.g. in the Nextcloud web UI) the write fails --
          re-read and retry deliberately rather than looping.
        - Pass the literal ``"*"`` to **force-overwrite** an existing
          file unconditionally (fails if the file does not exist).

Returns:
    ``WriteFileResponse`` with ``path``, ``status_code``, ``size``,
    ``created`` (True when a new file was created, i.e. HTTP 201, False
    when an existing file was overwritten, i.e. HTTP 204) and ``etag``.

    ``etag`` is the file as just written — pass it straight back as
    ``if_match`` on the next write to chain edits without an intervening
    read. It is ``None`` when the server did not return one (some
    proxies strip it). Re-read the file to obtain it in that case.
tools.name: nc_webdav_write_file

size.title: Size

created.description: Whether a new file was created (vs overwritten)
created.title: Created

etag.description: ETag of the file as written. Pass it straight back as `if_match` on the next write to chain edits without re-reading. None if the server did not return one (some proxies strip it) — re-read the file to obtain it in that case.
etag.title: Etag

tools.description:
Change part of a text file in place, by exact text replacement.

Prefer this over nc_webdav_write_file for changing an existing text
file: send only the passage to replace and its replacement, not the
whole file. Plain UTF-8 text files only, such as Markdown (including
Collectives pages), YAML, JSON, XML, CSV, configuration files and
source code. PDFs, Office and OpenDocument files, images other than
SVG, audio, video and archives are refused, because a text edit would
corrupt them. Replace those as a whole with nc_webdav_write_file.

Each edit replaces ``old_string`` with ``new_string``. ``old_string``
must match the file exactly, including whitespace, indentation and
line breaks, and must occur exactly once unless ``replace_all`` is
true, so quote enough surrounding text to make it unique. Strip the
line-number prefix if you copied the text from a read with
line_numbers. To delete text, use an empty ``new_string``.

Several edits are applied in order, each to the result of the previous
one, and saved as a single change (one new file version). If any edit
cannot be applied, nothing is saved and the error says which one and
why.

The file is read and written back guarded by its etag, so a change
made elsewhere at the same moment is never overwritten. Pass
``if_match`` (an etag from nc_webdav_read_file) to also refuse the edit
if the file changed since you read it. Windows line endings (CRLF) and
a byte-order mark are kept as they are.

Raises ``ToolError`` when the file does not exist, is not a plain UTF-8
text file, is larger than ``WEBDAV_WRITE_MAX_MB``, carries an excluded
tag, is locked, changed concurrently, or when an edit cannot be applied.

Args:
    path: Full path of the file to edit
    edits: Replacements, applied in order. Each has ``old_string``,
        ``new_string`` and optionally ``replace_all``.
    if_match: Optional etag from an earlier read. The edit fails if
        the file has changed since.

Returns:
    ``EditFileResponse`` with the new ``etag``, the number of
    ``replacements`` and a unified ``diff`` of the change, to check it
    without re-reading the file.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace, including whitespace, indentation and line breaks. Must occur exactly once unless replace_all is true.
old_string.title: Old String

new_string.description: Replacement text. An empty string deletes old_string.
new_string.title: New String

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of exactly one
replace_all.title: Replace All

tools.name: nc_webdav_edit_file

etag.description: ETag of the file as written. Pass it as if_match to the next edit or write to make sure nobody changed the file in between. None if the server did not return one.
etag.title: Etag

edits_applied.description: Number of edits applied, in order
edits_applied.title: Edits Applied

replacements.description: Occurrences replaced in total (more than edits_applied when replace_all matched several)
replacements.title: Replacements

size.description: Size of the file as written, in bytes
size.title: Size

diff.description: Unified diff of the change with two lines of context, to check it without re-reading the file
diff.title: Diff

diff_truncated.description: Whether the diff was cut short. The edit itself is complete.
diff_truncated.title: Diff Truncated

tools.description:
Create a short-lived, read-only public download link for a file.

Use this for binary files (especially images) the client needs as bytes
rather than as text: ``nc_webdav_read_file`` base64s anything it cannot
extract text from, which can exceed the MCP client response budget and get
truncated, leaving the file undecodable. (For documents -- PDF, DOCX --
prefer reading them: that tool returns their text or markdown.)
A public link keeps the MCP response small and lets the client download
the exact original bytes from ``download_url``.

The link is always **read-only** (``permissions=1``): a public,
anonymously-accessible link with write access would be a security
footgun, so it is intentionally not configurable. Use ``nc_share_create``
(shareType=3) if you genuinely need a writable public link.

Args:
    path: Path to the file to share (relative to your files, e.g.
        "/Receipts/receipt.jpg")
    expires_in_minutes: How long the link should remain valid, in
        minutes (default: 30). Must be positive — this tool only
        creates short-lived links, never a permanent one. See the
        expiry caveat below.

Expiry caveat:
    Nextcloud enforces public-link expiry at **date granularity**, not
    minute precision: a link expires at 00:00:00 on ``expireDate`` in
    the owner's timezone (i.e. the end of the day before ``expireDate``).
    The requested window is rounded up so the link stays valid at least
    that long. ``expires_at`` reports the precise requested instant, but
    the link may remain valid until the end of that day server-side. To
    revoke earlier, call ``nc_share_delete`` with the returned
    ``share_id``.

Returns:
    PublicDownloadLinkResponse with the share URL, download URL, and
    advisory expiry.

Raises:
    ToolError: If ``expires_in_minutes`` is not positive, or if the OCS
        response carries no share url.

Create a comprehensive calendar event with full feature support.

Args:
    calendar_name: Name of the calendar to create the event in
    title: Event title
    start_datetime: ISO format. Three modes:
        - ``"2025-01-15T14:00:00Z"`` or ``"2025-01-15T14:00:00+00:00"``
          → stored as UTC.
        - ``"2025-01-15T14:00:00"`` with ``timezone="America/New_York"``

          plus a VTIMEZONE component).

          local time (interpreted by viewers in their own zone). A
          warning is logged so the choice is visible.
        - ``"2025-01-15"`` for all-day events.
    ctx: MCP context
    end_datetime: ISO format end time, empty for all-day events
    all_day: Whether this is an all-day event
    description: Event description/details

    categories: Comma-separated categories (e.g., "work,meeting")

        ``recurrence_rule`` already implies recurrence, so leave this
        unset unless you want to suppress it with ``False``.

        ``recurrence_rule`` already carries ``UNTIL`` or ``COUNT``.

        ``ACTION:EMAIL``. Nextcloud addresses it to the event's
        attendees and the calendar's sharees.

tools.description:
Find available time slots for scheduling meetings.

Analyses the events in your calendars (and, for any attendees given,
their free/busy as reported by the server) and returns the gaps that
are long enough. Slots are *maximal* free windows: a free morning comes
back once as a single long slot, not as a grid of candidate start
times, so pick any sub-range of at least duration_minutes from one.

Not everything on a calendar consumes time. Events marked free
(TRANSP:TRANSPARENT), cancelled events, and calendars set to "never
show me as busy" are ignored. All-day events are ignored too unless
include_all_day is set, because birthdays, name days and subscribed
holiday feeds would otherwise blank out whole working days.

        should also be checked (RFC 6638, which requires a server that
        answers scheduling requests for them)

        defaulting to now. Never searches into the past.
    date_range_end: End date for availability search (YYYY-MM-DD),
        defaulting to a week after the start

    exclude_weekends: Skip Saturdays and Sundays
    preferred_times: Preferred time ranges as "HH:MM-HH:MM"

        rather than narrowing them. Overlapping ranges are merged, and

    timezone: IANA timezone the business hours and preferred times are
        expressed in, e.g. "Europe/Amsterdam". Defaults to the server's

tools.description:
Save an email as a draft WITHOUT sending it (requires mail.draft scope).

Nothing is delivered to anyone. The draft is written to the account's
Drafts mailbox (created as "Drafts" if the account has none), where the
user can review, edit and send it from Nextcloud Mail or any other mail
client. Use this to prepare a message, for example a reply, that a person
sends themselves.

The ``From:`` identity is derived by the Mail app from ``account_id``.
Recipients are arrays of ``{"label": "...", "email": "..."}`` objects
(``label`` is optional), as for nc_mail_send_message. Example for ``to``::

    [{"label": "John Doe", "email": "john@example.com"}]

recipients yourself. There is no reply-reference parameter: the Mail app
does not keep In-Reply-To/References on drafts it writes to the Drafts

tool. To revise one, save a new draft and ask the user to discard the old
one.

the marker.
